methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops led by a Norfolk native directly building peer-to-peer AI fluency in Hampton Roads signals grassroots capability distribution, demonstrating how local champions can activate deep learning networks outside traditional tech hubs.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab establishes institutional infrastructure for distributed AI education in Southwest Virginia, potentially seeding peer networks that could spread deep capability beyond metro concentration zones.

signals.title: Meta, Google invest in skilled worker training to build Virginia data centers - Axios
signals.signal_reading: Meta and Google investing in skilled worker training for Richmond-area data centers concentrates both capital and advanced workforce development in metro hubs, deepening capability gaps as tech giants anchor talent pipelines to infrastructure nodes rather than distributing expertise statewide.

signals.title: How Local Businesses in Virginia and West Virginia Can Use AI Consulting to Plan Smarter Automation - Williamson Daily News
signals.signal_reading: AI consulting services marketed to small businesses across Virginia and West Virginia signal platform-mediated adoption where businesses consume AI tools through intermediaries rather than building internal capability, creating broad but shallow engagement that reinforces vendor dependence.

signals.title: How Fairfax County police are using AI — and why opponents are concerned - NBC4 Washington
signals.signal_reading: Fairfax County police deploying AI capabilities demonstrates how concentrated resources in NoVA enable advanced implementation that rural jurisdictions cannot match, widening the public sector technology capability gap between regions with different resource bases.
